r: A eunuch slave seized at **Cambay** by **Nusrat Khan** in the **Gujarat campaign (1299)** and presented to Alauddin
His first master had **bought him for 1,000 dinars**
Rose to **Malik Naib**; **commander** of all of Alauddin's **Deccan campaigns**
Treaty and annual tribute; loot on 1,000 camels
**Wealth and tribute, not annexation** – "financial ventures" (K.S. Lal); annexation came only under **Muhammad bin Tughlaq**
Boldness and adventure; **untold wealth** brought to Delhi; **fresh geographical knowledge** of the south; Kafur's elevation as **Malik Naib**
A later popular tradition only; no contemporary record
Their line had already ended in **1279** under the Pandyas

First attack on Warangal by **Malik Fakhruddin Juna** (with Malik Chhajju) **failed at Upparapalli** – the **Kakatiya army defeated Alauddin's army**; victors **Potuganti Maili** and **Recherla Venna**
**Kafur** with **Khwaja Haji** besieged Warangal; **Amir Khusrau** went along – Khazain-ul-Futuh describes a **double-walled fort** with a **moat**
**Third invasion**, by **Khusrau Khan** under Mubarak Shah
**Chengiz Khan** reached the **Indus** under **Iltutmish**, chasing Mangbarni – the **first** Mongol threat; he **did not cross the Indus**
Beat a Mongol force under **Abdullah**; converts settled as "**New Mussalmans**"
**Battle of Kili** (third invasion of Alauddin's reign) – Mongols under **Qutlugh Khwaja**; **Zafar Khan killed** fighting them
**Amroha** – Ali Beg and Tartaq (Khwaja Tash) beaten by **Malik Kafur and Ghazi Malik**
Kabak beaten on the **Ravi** by Kafur and Ghazi Malik → **Ravi = Sultanate–Mongol boundary** after 1306

1.x: **Muhammad bin Tughluq** bought off **Tarmashirin** and lost no north-western territory to the Mongols.

**Defence:** repaired and built north-west forts (completing **Balban's** policy); new capital **Siri**; **large standing army**; **Ghazi Malik** warden of the marches, said to have beaten the Mongols **29** times.
**Zafar Khan** died at **Kili**; **Nusrat Khan** died at **Ranthambore**.

r: First conquest; **Ulugh Khan and Nusrat Khan**; **Somnath** plundered; queen **Kamala Devi** taken; Kafur acquired
Raided on the way to Gujarat
First main target in Rajasthan; first siege 1299 failed, **Nusrat Khan killed**; Alauddin took it in person

2.x: **Events in order:** **Gujarat (1299) → Mongols under Ali Beg and Tartaq (1305) → Kafur sacks the Pandyas (1311) → Yadava kingdom annexed (1313 by Kafur; finally 1318)**.
**Policy:** **North annexed**; **south** – kings kept their thrones and **paid tribute**.
**First Turkish invasion of the south:** Alauddin's **Devagiri** raid (**1296**), as governor of Kara.

r: **Ulugh Khan, Nusrat Khan, Zafar Khan, Ain-ul-Mulk Multani, Malik Kafur, Ghazi Malik**; court poet **Amir Khusrau**
World conquest and a **new religion** – dropped on the advice of the **Kotwal Ala-ul-Mulk** (Barani's uncle)
Told **Qazi Mughisuddin of Bayana** he acted in the **interest of the state**, not by the ulema; revived **Balban's** harsh centralised rule without religious sanction
Separated **Shariat** from **Zawabit** (state laws made by the ruler)
Built by **Alauddin Khalji** (distinct from the Kakatiya Thousand Pillar temple)

4.x: **Two Khizr Khans:** Alauddin's son (set aside 1316) and the Sayyid Sultan are different persons.

r: **Kafur** set aside Khizr Khan and enthroned the minor **Shihabuddin Umar** → Kafur killed

**Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah**, last Khalji – the only surviving member of Alauddin's family; **withdrew his father's harsh regulations**, restored confiscated lands, **abolished the price control system**; murdered by **Khusrau Khan** (Nasiruddin Khusrau Shah)
**Ghazi Malik**, Alauddin's general and governor of the Punjab, killed Khusrau Khan and became **Ghiyasuddin Tughluq** – **first Tughlaq Sultan**

5.x: **1303:** Alauddin defeated **Rana Ratan Singh**; his wife **Rani Padmini** and the Rajput women performed **jauhar**.
**Muhammad Shah (1719-48):** first Mughal ruler to patronise **Urdu**.
**Debate:** Padmavat was written over two centuries later; many historians treat the Padmini motive as legend.

r: **First Sultan with a benevolent attitude to Hindus**; lenient to rebels such as **Malik Chhajju**
Married his daughter to **Ulugh Khan**, a descendant of **Chengiz Khan**; settled Mongol converts as **New Mussalmans**
**Murdered at Kara (1296)** by his nephew and son-in-law **Alauddin**
